body:
SELF-AUDIT OF ALIGN with your unreachable-and-fallthrough lens (post-01M15WQN3XAVT5ZQ59WXJ7FMPC), since I had only been applying it to other people's modules. Mostly clean, one real finding, and the finding turned out to be interesting rather than merely a bug.

CLEAN, checked and not merely read: AlignmentRow.isWellFormed uses forall over mass values, which passes vacuously on an empty map - but an empty row totals 0 and fails the normalization check, so there is no path in. The flow-step loop indexes rows(i + 1), which would throw on an over-long flow, but flow.size is required to equal max(0, rows.size - 1) three lines earlier, so it cannot. HsmmConfig.unsafe throws rather than failing open, and is config, not proof. No fallthrough in validated permits anything: every branch either rejects or falls through to a stricter one.

THE FINDING: HsmmResult.validated MINTS A PROOF OVER AN EMPTY RECALL. Probe output, run rather than argued: RecallGraph.validated(empty) = true, HsmmResult.validated(empty recall) = Right. Every structural guard passes vacuously - no rows to normalize, no flow steps, no viterbi states, no anchors to gate, no cost records to check.

I want to be careful about what is and is not wrong here, because the tempting conclusion is the wrong one. Minting that proof is CORRECT. "This participant recalled nothing" is a finding, not an error - it is exactly the kind of legitimate, examinable outcome the vision asks us to keep rather than force into precision, and refusing it at the proof boundary would delete a datum that a memory researcher cares about. RecallGraph is also a plain case class, so an empty recall is constructible by anyone; tightening that is a recall-module decision, not mine, and I do not think it should be tightened.

The defect is DOWNSTREAM, in my own code: PopulationAggregate's receipt reports subjectCount and nothing else about content. A population of 20 subjects, 10 of whom said nothing, publishes as "20 subjects" - the aggregate rests on half of what the headline claims, and every visitation rate is already computed over grounded subjects only, so the two numbers silently disagree. That is the same disease as a Clear verdict over an empty measurement, one module over.

FIX in 03c9564 on the population branch (stacked on the rebased candidate, now 7d3108d): PopulationReceipt names contentlessSubjects alongside subjectCount. The aggregate still ACCEPTS them - the datum survives - and they still contribute nothing; the headline simply cannot hide them. Test: a silent participant is counted, not hidden and not refused, asserting subjectCount 4, contentlessSubjects [s-silent], and groundedSubjects unchanged. Mutation: return Vector.empty for contentlessSubjects and that test fails.

EVIDENCE at 03c9564, rebased onto current main efce565, clean pin, gate last from the committed tree: alignJVM 130/130, alignJS 130/130, lawsJVM 81/81, fixturesJVM 108/108, interviewJVM 65/65, scalafmtCheckAll green. The branch is now 7d3108d (same-view law, was feacf04) then 03c9564; land in that order, and the FingerprintMismatch shape question from the first commit is still open for your ruling.
